stage_2_story.text_en:
Moshe's grandson Yonatan, who is now sixteen and plays for his school team, sat down with his grandfather at halftime during a big Maccabi Tel Aviv EuroLeague match to explain what he had observed in the first half.

'Saba,' Yonatan began, 'did you see how they used the zone defence in the first quarter? Instead of each player guarding one opponent, they covered areas of the court. It confused Hapoel's guards completely.'

Moshe nodded slowly. 'But then Hapoel's big man set a screen near the arc and the shooter stepped behind it and scored a three-pointer. That surprised them.'

Yonatan was impressed. 'Exactly! Maccabi's switch was too slow. The defenders called out to swap opponents, but the shooter already had a clean release before anyone got close.'

Moshe pointed at the screen: 'And that play where one player throws the ball up and the other one jumps to catch it above the basket — what is that called?'

'That is an alley-oop,' said Yonatan. 'It is hard to defend because you need perfect timing between the two players.'

In the final minute, Maccabi called an isolation play for their star guard, who went one-on-one and scored. The other team responded with an aggressive foul — the referee called it a flagrant foul and awarded two free throws and possession.

By the final buzzer, Maccabi's star player had recorded a triple-double. Moshe shook his head in amazement. 'You know, Yonatan, when I understand the game, it is much more exciting.' Yonatan smiled. 'That is why I explain it to you, Saba.'

questions.question: Who explained the basketball tactics to Moshe in this story?
What defensive system did Maccabi use in the first quarter?
How did Hapoel score against the zone defence?
options: (a) With an alley-oop from the baseline
(c) A shooter stepped behind the arc after a screen and scored a three-pointer
(d) Their centre scored inside after a fast break

questions.question: Why did Maccabi's switch fail on that play?
options: (a) The defender slipped on the court
(b) The switch was too slow and the shooter had a clean release before anyone got close
(c) The coach called a timeout too late

questions.question: What did Moshe ask Yonatan about?
options: (b) The isolation play at the end
(c) The play where one player throws the ball up and another catches it above the basket

questions.question: What is an alley-oop, according to Yonatan?
options: (a) A defensive play that requires a switch
(b) A play that requires perfect timing between two players, where the ball is thrown up and caught above the basket
(c) A foul called by the referee near the arc
(d) A type of isolation move for the best scorer

questions.question: What play did Maccabi call in the final minute?
options: (c) An isolation play for their star guard

questions.question: What did the referee award after the flagrant foul?
options: (a) One free throw and a warning
(d) A player was ejected and no free throws were awarded

questions.question: What did Maccabi's star player achieve by the end of the game?
options: (c) He set a screen that broke the zone defence

questions.question: What did Moshe say at the end of the story?
options: (a) He said basketball was still too complicated
(c) He said the game is much more exciting when he understands it
(d) He said Yonatan should become a coach
